title: Align SLA language with tiered SLO measurement + define SLO→SLA mapping (Hosted vs Dedicated)
creator: Evelyn Hart
description:
Objective
Finalize customer-facing SLA language and internal SLO→SLA mapping so that (a) contracts reflect what we can measure and enforce, (b) exclusions match SLI filters, and (c) CS/Sales can explain incidents and credits consistently.

This ticket is part of the Tiered SLO + Error Budget program. Customers are asking for clear definitions of what counts against uptime/latency, especially around burst traffic (overload shedding), streaming disconnects, and fallback behavior.

Scope
- Hosted API (shared) SLA wording + definitions (baseline).
- Dedicated capacity SLA wording + definitions (primary focus, enterprise contracts).
- Mapping document that explicitly ties:
  1) internal SLIs/SLO windows (rolling 28d or calendar month) → 2) contractual SLA measurement window and credit math → 3) exclusions/filters.
- Enablement artifacts for CS/Solutions Engineering: "what counts" decision tree + example customer Q&A.

Out of scope (this phase)
- Private / on-prem SLA commitments (capture as future work; reference only).
- Changing underlying SLO targets (owned in PM-812; this ticket consumes approved targets).

Inputs / references
- Confluence: product-docs/requirements/tiered-slo-to-sla-mapping-hosted-and-dedicated
- Confluence: eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/tiered-slo-definitions-hosted-vs-dedicated
- Confluence: eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/error-budget-policy-and-enforcement
- Recent customer questions motivating this: SUP-28412 (Dedicated SLO/error budget reporting), SUP-28501 (Hosted streaming disconnect accounting)

Key decisions we must nail down (language must match measurement)
1) Availability definition
- Internal SLI: request success rate (non-5xx) with explicit exclusions.
- Proposed SLA definition: "Successful Requests / Total Valid Requests" where Valid excludes invalid auth, malformed payloads, and customer-side aborts.
- Align phrasing so we do not promise on events we intentionally exclude (rate-limited, invalid, client abort).

2) Latency commitments (Dedicated)
- Dedicated contracts often ask for p95 latency commitments; our SLOs are per-endpoint + region and may differ by model class.
- We should avoid model-specific commitments in contract unless we can freeze model/version and isolate load (risk of constant renegotiation).
- Proposed contract stance:
  - Contract states latency SLO applies to "Supported Models" on "Dedicated Capacity" in "Covered Regions"; details enumerated in Order Form or product addendum.
  - If we must include a number, include a single p95 threshold per endpoint class with clear exclusions and measurement point.

3) Streaming reliability
- Internal SLI: streaming disconnect/error events; exclude explicit client disconnects and timeouts attributable to client network where detectable.
- Contract language needs clarity: credits apply when Redwood terminates stream unexpectedly or fails to deliver tokens after stream established (server-side).
- Open question: how to handle proxy/load balancer resets that appear as disconnect but are partially out of app control; we need observable taxonomy from SRE/Telemetry.

4) Exclusions / filters (must match SLI spec)
We need a single authoritative list used in:
- SLA definitions (customer-facing)
- CS escalation template
- Incident comms language

Candidate exclusions (tentative; confirm with SRE + Legal):
- Invalid requests: 4xx due to customer auth, malformed inputs, exceeding max limits.
- Rate limiting / quotas: 429 and related policy rejections.
- Customer-initiated aborts / disconnects (where request context indicates client cancellation).
- Scheduled maintenance with prior notice (define notice period).
- Force majeure / upstream cloud provider outages (careful: keep narrow; don’t overreach).
- Beta/preview features or non-GA models (must be labeled in catalog/contract).

5) Graceful degradation / fallback behavior
- We need contract-safe wording about routing/fallback during partial outages.
- Dedicated: we generally should not fail over Dedicated traffic to Hosted unless explicitly agreed (data isolation + performance).
- If we do allow failover (same customer, alternate region or alternate pool), the contract should define whether fallback counts as "service available" for SLA purposes (likely yes if request served within documented compatibility + within latency, but must be aligned with SLI accounting).

Deliverables
A) SLO→SLA mapping doc (Confluence) with:
- Definitions (Availability, Latency where applicable, Streaming)
- Measurement windows and aggregation method (calendar month vs rolling)
- What counts / what is excluded (single list)
- How credits are calculated and what evidence we provide (dashboards/export)
- Examples: 3–5 common customer scenarios with how they’re classified

B) Contract-ready language pack (for Legal/Sales Ops)
- Dedicated addendum wording: definitions + measurement + exclusions + credit schedule.
- Hosted API baseline SLA wording: keep simpler; ensure it matches the same core definitions.

C) Enablement
- CS/Solutions Engineering one-pager: escalation expectations, what to collect, and how to interpret SLO dashboards.
- Sales enablement bullets: how to answer "Is this an SLA or SLO?", "Do streaming disconnects count?", "What about burst traffic?"

Stakeholders
- Product: Evelyn Hart (CPO), Nikhil Sharma (Hosted), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated)
- Eng/SRE: Sean Gallagher, Aisha Bello
- CS/SE: Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim, Markus Klein
- Docs: Elliot Price (customer-facing docs lead)
- Legal/Sales Ops: TBD (loop in once draft is coherent)

Open questions (need answers before we finalize wording)
- Confirm official SLA window (calendar month strongly preferred for contracts; can map from internal rolling 28d in reporting).
- Confirm which latency percentile(s) we are comfortable supporting contractually for Dedicated (p95 only vs p95+p99; endpoint scope).
- Confirm streaming disconnect taxonomy and what is reliably detectable as client-side vs server-side.
- Confirm whether 5xx during overload shedding count (they should count; policy should be to shed with 429/503? SRE needs to confirm behavior and how it’s logged).
- Confirm how retries are treated in SLI (single attempt vs eventual success). Contract should measure request outcome, not internal retries.

Risks
- Mismatch between contract language and telemetry can create credit disputes.
- Overly broad exclusions will be rejected by procurement; overly narrow exclusions create financial risk.
- Dedicated customers expect isolation; any cross-tier fallback must be explicitly described and controlled.

Next steps (this week)
- Pull latest SLI exclusion list from ENG-4921 outputs and the SLI spec.
- Draft a single exclusion list and get SRE + CS sign-off.
- Draft Dedicated SLA addendum text in a doc for Legal review.
- Schedule a 45-min review with Product/SRE/CS/SE to validate wording against real scenarios (streaming, overload, region failover).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Confluence mapping doc is published and linked from the reliability program hub; includes definitions, exclusions, and 3+ worked examples.
2) Dedicated SLA addendum draft is reviewed by SRE (Aisha Bello) and CS (Rachel Kim) for measurability + customer clarity.
3) Hosted SLA language is updated (or explicitly confirmed unchanged) to match the same core definitions and exclusion terms.
4) Sales/CS enablement one-pager is delivered to Jasmine Liu + Markus Klein with an agreed escalation script and customer Q&A.
5) Any remaining open questions are tracked as follow-up tickets with owners and dates (e.g., streaming taxonomy gaps, calendar-month vs rolling window reporting).
comments: 2026-02-03 — Lauren Bishop: Drafted initial exclusion list based on current SLI spec. Biggest contention: whether to exclude provider-level networking issues; recommending we keep force majeure language narrow and only for verified upstream regional outages. Scheduling review with Aisha + Rachel.

2026-02-06 — Aisha Bello: Confirmed internal SLI filters: exclude invalid (4xx schema/auth), exclude 429 rate limits, exclude client aborts when cancellation is explicit in gateway logs. 5xx always count. For overload shedding we should prefer 429/503; classification depends on final routing behavior + telemetry (ENG-4922).

2026-02-07 — Rachel Kim: Need a customer-friendly explanation for streaming disconnects: "if Redwood ends the stream unexpectedly" vs customer network. Suggest we add an example section and align with SUP-28501 learnings; also need a standard evidence package (dashboard screenshot + request IDs) for credit claims.

2026-02-10 — Nikhil Sharma: Hosted language should avoid latency guarantees; keep latency as internal SLO for ops and publish only availability SLA for Hosted. Dedicated can include latency commitment but must be endpoint-class scoped and not model-specific unless pinned in the order form.

2026-02-12 — Markus Klein: Sales needs a short talk track: difference between SLO and SLA, what dashboards customers get on Dedicated, and how error budgets relate (internal control, not contractual credit). Please ensure we explicitly say error budget is an internal reliability mechanism.

2026-02-14 — Lauren Bishop: Incorporated feedback; moving toward a calendar-month SLA window with internal reporting mapped from rolling windows. Waiting on Legal to confirm credit table format and notice-period language for scheduled maintenance.
